database.qualificationLaw: Every application and compatibility relation reference is schema-qualified. No writable schema precedes pg_catalog or ci_coordinator in a runtime search_path.

isolationEnforcement.verificationPhase: first statement after begin and before timeouts or fence acquisition

snapshotReadIsolationEnforcement.verificationPhase: before fence acquisition and schema-dependent admission
snapshotReadIsolationEnforcement.snapshotBoundary: The shared compatibility fence precedes current-revision admission; all jointly interpreted bounded projections and metadata use one subsequent statement snapshot under READ COMMITTED plus READ ONLY.

fence.keyDerivation: first eight SHA-256 bytes split into two signed big-endian int32 values
fence.snapshotLaw: Fence acquisition and current-revision admission are separate SQL statements. Under READ COMMITTED, the admission statement observes a snapshot created after the fence is acquired.
fence.lockOrder: compatibility fence before capability-owned table, row, or advisory locks

timeoutProfiles.cancellationLaw: SQLSTATE 57014 is query_canceled and does not identify statement_timeout provenance. Caller task cancellation remains observable and is never rewritten as a timeout.

fence.invariant: No schema-dependent statement may execute before the transaction holds the shared compatibility fence and admits its required capabilities. Every migration transaction holds the exclusive compatibility fence before compatibility-relevant DDL or declaration changes.

declaration.continuityLaw: Bootstrap is the induction base. Each first application validates exactly the current declaration and its proposed successor, while database uniqueness, parent foreign-key, generation, and immutability constraints preserve the historical induction hypothesis. Runtime admission never loads the unbounded history.
declaration.ordering: generation-ascending and capability-id UTF-8 byte order
declaration.idempotentReplay: An existing revision is accepted only when every declaration field, capability row, and declaration hash is byte-equivalent to the proposed declaration.
declaration.immutability: UPDATE and DELETE are rejected by database triggers; the runtime principal has SELECT only on declaration relations.

expand.law: previous.providedCapabilities is a proper subset of next.providedCapabilities
expand.resultingCapabilityLaw: Every capability in next.providedCapabilities, including every retained capability, must attest against the resulting schema and data state.

contract.law: next.providedCapabilities is a proper subset of previous.providedCapabilities
contract.resultingCapabilityLaw: Every capability in next.providedCapabilities must attest against the resulting schema and data state.

capabilityAdmission.relation: required capability identifiers and descriptor hashes are an exact subset of currentDeclaration.providedCapabilities
capabilityAdmission.requiredCapabilities: non-empty sorted unique exact capability identifiers
capabilityAdmission.cacheLaw: A positive schema attestation may be reused only for the same cache key while the transaction holds the shared fence.
capabilityAdmission.requiredSetOwner: Each schema-dependent operation contract owns one immutable non-empty required capability set. A use case may only union the sets of operations it invokes and cannot narrow them.

dataCompatibility.capabilityIdentityLaw: A capability identifier has immutable schema, data-domain, codec, backfill, routine, and privilege semantics across all code artifacts. Any semantic change requires a new identifier.
dataCompatibility.mixedVersionLaw: Retained rows must remain in the intersection of every retained reader domain, and the union of rows producible by retained writers must be a subset of the intersection of retained reader domains.
dataCompatibility.bridgeConstraintLaw: Before mixed deployment, validated PostgreSQL constraints must prove every retained row and every future write lies inside every retained reader domain. If the domain cannot be expressed and enforced by the admitted database constraint algebra, the transition is outside the cooperative rolling protocol.
dataCompatibility.backfillLaw: A capability whose read or write domain depends on a backfill cannot attest until the declared backfill state is complete and independently verified.
dataCompatibility.seededWitnessRole: Seeded boundary rows are falsifiers for codecs and constraints; finite examples are never authority for universal domain inclusion.

schemaAttestation.factOwner: schema_attestation.py reads bounded PostgreSQL catalog and effective-privilege facts only
schemaAttestation.dataFactOwner: data_attestation.py attests validated capability-owned bridge constraints and executes bounded seeded-row and backfill falsifiers
schemaAttestation.policyOwner: schema_capabilities.py is a pure capability requirement registry and performs no SQL
requiredPlanes: retained data read and write domains
per-session exact runtime grants before repository exposure

schemaEvolution.additiveCompatibility: A new relation or object outside every retained capability-owned closure may be compatible. A changed column, constraint, index, trigger, policy, storage fact, or privilege inside a retained closure requires a new capability and cannot be inferred compatible from DDL syntax.
schemaEvolution.unknownDisjointObjects: permitted when no retained capability attestation selects them

runtimePrincipal: cannot CREATE in the application schema
has no grant options or role memberships; all capability grants are direct
migrationPrincipal: owns the application schema and compatibility objects
is not used by the runtime service
publicPrincipal: has no CREATE on the application schema
has no privileges on application or compatibility relations, routines, independently grantable types or domains, or array types through their element type
privilegeModel.defaultPrivilegePolicy: No committed schema, relation, sequence, function, procedure, type, or domain privilege may be available to PUBLIC. Migrations do not mutate role-global defaults; they revoke object privileges in the creating transaction and reject schema-local PUBLIC defaults. PostgreSQL array types reject independent ACL changes and derive effective USAGE from their element type, so raw ACL attestation selects typelem = 0 and effective principal attestation covers the complete type closure. The runtime principal has no default ACL entries and receives reviewed direct grants only.
privilegeModel.roleAttributePolicy: Runtime roles must be direct-login non-superuser, non-replication, non-bypass-RLS, non-role-creation, and non-database-creation principals with no pg_auth_members membership rows.

identityEvidence.membershipLaw: no pg_auth_members row where member = session_user
identityEvidence.grantLaw: runtime capability grants are direct, exact, and non-grantable
identityEvidence.attestationPhase: migration declaration attests static post-DDL facts; each runtime transaction separately attests exact session-principal grants after the shared fence and declaration admission before repository exposure

migrationExecution.fencePhaseLaw: Acquire the exclusive fence inside the outer migration transaction before current-head inspection, context.run_migrations, revision DDL, or declaration writes.

runtimeDatabaseBoundary.law: Schema-dependent runtime code receives repositories only from the compatibility-admitted unit of work; raw engines and sessions are not public persistence exports.
runtimeDatabaseBoundary.cooperationNonClaim: Database privileges prevent runtime DDL and declaration mutation but cannot force advisory-lock participation by arbitrary SQL clients.

readinessProjection.consistencyLaw: The shared compatibility fence prevents migration, not ordinary domain writes. Readiness verifies immutable audit rows through its initial head, then observes the final head and maximum sequence together in one statement. A valid advancing head retains the verified prefix as progress; an unchanged consistent head admits that prefix without domain-row locks.
readinessProjection.nonClaim: A passed readiness projection is not authority for a later schema-dependent transaction.

rollout.cooperativeClientPrecondition: Every supported schema-dependent client participates in the fence protocol and the runtime principal cannot perform DDL or declaration mutation.
rollout.rollbackLaw: Code rollback is admissible only when every capability required by the rollback target is provided by the current declared revision and its code-owned schema attestation passes under the shared fence.
rollout.artifactProofLaw: A rollback-capability claim requires execution of an immutable artifact identified by the exact predecessor source commit and artifact digest against the post-transition database. An artifact built from current source before a test-owned transition proves only that transition and is not predecessor-release evidence.

forwardMigrationProtocol.firstApplication: Append exactly one bootstrap, expand, or contract successor declaration atomically with DDL and Alembic head movement.
forwardMigrationProtocol.knownRevisionReplay: Byte-exactly validate the existing declaration and append nothing.

rollout.migrationDowngradeLaw: Before retained production state, downgrade under the exclusive fence may select and byte-exactly validate an already declared ancestor without appending a declaration. After retention, compatibility corrections are forward-only unless a separately admitted destructive-data protocol proves otherwise.

proofRouting.nonClaim: Native routes and the canonical mutation inventory identify local witnesses; they do not prove provider execution, deployment, or production database state.

nonClaims: This profile does not make advisory locks mandatory for clients that have not adopted this protocol.
This profile does not protect against a superuser, schema owner, or non-cooperating migration that intentionally bypasses the protocol.
This profile does not prove zero-downtime deployment, backup, restore, replication, failover, capacity, or production readiness.
This profile does not authorize a contract transition or removal of a capability merely because the transition shape is valid.
This profile does not prove advisory-key collision freedom or migration starvation freedom against unrelated or non-cooperating database clients.
